newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine trade says USDA maize figure too low.
newsitem.headline: Argentine trade says USDA maize figure too low.

text.p: Argentine traders said Friday they thought the U.S. Department of Agriculture's figure for 1996/97 maize output was too low.
The USDA predicted Argentine maize output at 12.5 million tonnes. It said it estimated wheat output of 14 million tonnes and soybean production of 13.5 million tonnes.
"The maize figure seems way on the low side to me, especially after all the recent rain," said one trader in Buenos Aires, "We think there could be 14.5 million tonnes or even 15 million tonnes."
Another trader was more cautious, but agreed that the USDA prediction was off: "I expect at least around 13 million tonnes, as long as the weather stays good."

A wave of wet weather in recent weeks has transformed what was a worrying situation of incipient drought in northern and inland zones of the grain belt, leaving the ploughlands with ample moisture for preparation sowing.

The Argentine government's Agricultural Secretariat said Thursday that farmers had sown 18.4 percent of an intended total of 3.8 million hectares with maize by October 4. The predicted total area is 10.6 percent higher than the area last season, when output was 10.5 million tonnes.
The Secretariat reckons output will be 13 million tonnes.
The rain also improved the already good state of the wheat crop in the south, and went a small way to repairing the damage of the dry spell in the north.

Traders were optimistic that wheat production would at least match the USDA forecast, which is 500,000 tonnes below the Argentine government figure. Traders' estimates ran from 14 million tonnes up to 15 million tonnes.
Traders more or less agreed with the USDA on soybeans, although one said he thought it was 500,000 tonnes too high. Soybean sowing is not due to get going for another month.
Long range weather forecasts are predicting the good crop weather to continue, with plenty of rain sweeping off the southern oceans in the next few months, traders said.
Argentine farmers produced 9.2 million tonnes of wheat in drought-blighted 1995/96. They also produced 12.5 million tonnes of soybeans and 5.6 million tonnes of sunflower seed.
Sunflower output this year is set to fall, with farmers opting for maize and wheat. One trader was predicting output of 5.3 million tonnes, the same as the government's forecast.
